title: Frontend app shell/navigation — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #62 (frontend-app-shell-navigation), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: AppShell.tsx wraps a `<Box component="nav">` around NavDrawer, whose own root is `<List component="nav" aria-label="main navigation">` — this nests two `<nav>` landmarks inside each other on every render (desktop and mobile), which is discouraged by ARIA authoring practices and reads as duplicate/confusing navigation to a screen-reader user jumping by landmark. Drop `component="nav"` from one of the two (the outer Box is only a layout wrapper for width/flex sizing; the semantic `<nav>` belongs on NavDrawer's List).

AppShell.test.tsx re-declares its own `mockMatchMedia` MediaQueryList mock object almost field-for-field identical to the default mock already installed in tests/setup.ts. Extract a shared helper (e.g. exported from tests/setup.ts or a small test-utils module) so future tests needing the narrow-width override don't have to keep two copies in sync.

Reconsider AppErrorBoundary's placement under components/layout/ vs components/common/. It satisfies Frontend.md §3's common/ criterion (doesn't reference a position/ticker/signal — fully domain-agnostic), and an error-boundary wrapper is a generically reusable pattern in its own right (could later wrap an individual feature subtree, not just the whole app) even though it's only instantiated once today — the task's own decisions entry leaned on 'used once, same pattern as AppShell' as the rationale for layout/, which is exactly the instantiation-count reasoning that doesn't establish non-reusability. Revisit once frontend-common-components lands and common/'s Storybook conventions (including a story that deliberately throws to exercise the fallback) are established, to decide with those conventions in hand rather than pre-empting them.
